subject: Customer LLM training, opt-out & retention — Pinebridge request
messages:
From: Sarah James <sarah.james@pinebridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@pinebridge.com>
Date: 2026-04-18T09:12:00-04:00
Subject: Inquiry — use of customer prompts for training, retention & DPIA

Hi Rishi,

We're reviewing vendors that surface AI capabilities to our customer-facing portals. Before we proceed with a pilot we need written confirmation on a few privacy items so our DPO can complete a DPIA:

1) Do you train models (foundation or fine-tune) on customer prompts/responses by default? If not, what is the opt-in process?
2) What are your default retention windows for prompt and response logs (for debugging/quality/eval)? Is there an option to turn that off or configure retention per tenant?
3) Where is customer content stored (region/proVIDER) and how do you handle cross-border transfers (SCCs or adequacy)?
4) Can you provide SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ evidence and a draft DPA we can review?

I've attached our DPIA template to help focus the answers (Pinebridge_DPIA_template.pdf). Ideally we need an initial response and any artifacts before our legal review next Friday.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if easier.

Best,
Sarah James
Data Protection Officer
Pinebridge Financial
Attach: Pinebridge_DPIA_template.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah James <sarah.james@pinebridge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-18T11:05:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — use of customer prompts for training, retention & DPIA

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear list and the DPIA template. Looping in Neha (Security & Privacy) and Lauren (Account lead) so we can coordinate artifacts and next steps. Summary answers below and I attached a short one-page data-use summary (redwood-llm-data-use-summary.pdf) to start.

High-level answers (short):
- Training on customer data: By default, Redwood does NOT use customer prompts or responses to further train or update our foundation models. Any contribution of customer data to model training is opt-in and requires explicit contractual consent (opt-in checkbox + DPA amendment).
- Opt-out / tenant controls: Customers can opt-out globally via the Redwood Console or via an API flag; we will also accept a signed DPA clause to enforce the opt-out.
- Retention windows: Default retention for request/response logs used for debugging/quality is 30 days. Logs are encrypted at rest and access is tightly logged. Customers can request retention reductions (24 hours) or disable request logging for their tenant (note: disabling logging limits our ability to support and debug).
- Data residency & transfers: Customer content for hosted deployments is stored in the region selected at provisioning (we support us/eu/apac regions). For cross-border transfers we rely on SCCs and provide a signed SCC statement; private deployments keep data in-customer-control (VPC/on-prem).
- Evidence & artifacts: We can provide SOC 2 Type II report (summary + redacted controls), completed SIG profile, CAIQ snapshot, and our standard DPA.

Attachments: redwood-llm-data-use-summary.pdf (summary), link to SOC2 & SIG to follow.

Proposed next steps:
- Neha will draft a DPIA response addressing Pinebridge template items (ETA 3 business days).
- Legal (Lauren) will share our DPA and an SCC statement.
- If helpful, schedule a 30-min call with Neha to walk the DPIA and technical flows.

Would you like to schedule that call tomorrow or early next week?

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
Attach: redwood-llm-data-use-summary.pdf
From: Sarah James <sarah.james@pinebridge.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal.ops@pinebridge.com>
Date: 2026-04-19T08:30:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — use of customer prompts for training, retention & DPIA

Thanks Rishi — that helps. A few follow-ups from our DPO:

- We will need a draft DPIA that maps data flows, subprocessors, retention controls, and deletion/erasure processes for EU subjects. Your 3-business-day ETA works; please include technical diagrams where possible.
- For SCCs: we need wording that confirms Redwood will act as processor and will execute the standard contractual clauses for transfers where applicable.
- For SOC 2: please include which controls cover encryption of data at rest (key management), access reviews (employee access), and secure deletion. Redactions are fine.
- Please share your standard DPA with any optional clauses clearly marked (training opt-in, telemetry retention).

I've attached our DPIA template again for reference. Proposed timeline: receive DPIA draft + DPA + SCC statement by 2026-04-23 so our legal can complete the review. If you cannot meet that, please propose an alternate date.

Also: we require a short call where your security lead can answer questions about access logging and deletion procedures. Can Neha join?

Best,
Sarah
Attach: Pinebridge_DPIA_template.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah James <sarah.james@pinebridge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-04-20T15:22:00-04:00
Subject: Re: Inquiry — use of customer prompts for training, retention & DPIA

Sarah — confirmed. We escalated to Security and Legal this morning. Next steps and deliverables:

1) DPIA draft: Neha will produce a DPIA response mapped to your template, including a data flow diagram and subprocessors list (ETA: 2026-04-23 EOD).
2) DPA & SCCs: Attached is our latest DPA draft (Redwood_DPA_v3.2.docx) with the training opt-in clause clearly marked; SCCs statement also attached (SCCs_statement.txt). Legal will accept redline requests.
3) SOC 2 / SIG / CAIQ: We will provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary and a completed SIG profile by 2026-04-23.
4) Call: I've proposed a 30-min slot here: https://cal.com/rishi/redwood-privacy-30 — Neha can join the call to discuss access logging, key management, and deletion workflows.

A couple clarifications to set expectations:
- Opt-in for model training requires explicit contractual consent and is not reversible for historical aggregated training runs; we will document the exact data handling in the DPA amendment.
- When tenants disable request logging, we mark those tenants as support-limited — some remedial actions will require a temporary opt-in for logs or provided debug snapshots under strict controls.

If that timeline works I will confirm once Neha uploads the DPIA draft. Thanks for the fast turnaround here.

-Rishi
